value.name: finds no codicil in cabinet
value.description: The search turns up no green folder or codicil in the cabinet, disappointing the group.
evidence: There were no green folders containing anything resembling a codicil.

value.name: group returns to front hall
value.description: The four people come back downstairs and gather in the front hall after the unsuccessful search.
evidence: They came back down the stairs. The four of them stood in the front hall

value.name: Daniel presses for answer
value.description: Daniel pauses at the newel post and prompts the others with a terse 'Well,' signaling impatience.
evidence:
Daniel had his hand on the newel post.

"Well," he said.

value.name: Asha reports no codicil found
value.description: Asha states that there is no codicil in the house so far and that she will continue searching.
evidence: "It means," Asha said, "that there is no codicil here. It does not mean there is no codicil. It means I have not found it in the places one would expect to find it. It means I am going to keep looking."

value.name: Daniel refuses prolonged search
value.description: Daniel objects that he has buyers, a written offer, taxes due, and an unpaid roofer, and says he cannot keep the house in limbo while Asha searches.
evidence: "Counselor." He said the word with a flatness that was not quite contempt but was not quite anything else either. "I have buyers. I have an offer in writing as of yesterday afternoon. I have property taxes due at the end of next month and I have a roofer who has called me three times about a repair my mother authorized in November and never paid for. I cannot keep this house in stasis while you turn over every cushion in the building looking for a piece of paper that no one in this room has actually seen."

value.name: Asha cites Rosa's sighting
value.description: When Daniel dismisses the codicil, Asha insists that Rosa has seen it before.

value.name: Rosa remains unshaken
value.description: Rosa does not react to the accusation or skepticism, and Asha notes her resilience.
evidence: The sentence sat in the hallway. Rosa did not flinch. She had been called worse things in her life, Asha thought, by people
